I have been using it a little bit over a year. It’s simple to use and really user friendly. I am no personal trainer nor a gym rat, i am just an average person at the gym and this app has helped me lose 42 pounds. 

One thing I would like to see as a feature would be to allow users to add their training goals and have the app create a training program based on that. For example if preparing for a marathon, spartan race or some sort of PT Test. 

AI chats do that nowadays and I could just copy and paste it to the app to keep track of the performance, but then it loses the reason for having the app.

reviews.title: I’m sure that it is a great app…
reviews.text: …once you learn how to use it.  To me, personally, it’s just not user friendly to me.  Maybe it’s me but I cannot figure out where to log everything.  I log it in one place the rest timer timer doesn’t start, I push a button (which one I don’t know?) and another place to log pops up and then, when I think I”m finished, I press the forward error, it doesn’t go to the next exercise and asks me if I want to save changes permanently.  I don’t know.  Then, at the end of the workout, instead of showing all six exercises that I started with, it showed two. It’s just not easy unless you memorize the “owners manual” before using.  I prefer not to have to stop my routine after every exercise to figure out how to log my sets/reps.  Might as well get out the notebook that I use to use in the early 90’s.  It’s faster…

reviews.title: OCD?
reviews.text:
I love measuring progress… and failures. How else do you know if you’re successful or not?  KPIs in business?  Absolutely.  That’s how I successfully built my company. In this app: How many workouts this month?  How much did I lift; how many days did I work out?  Yep.  Track it; refine it; see and measure the progress.  The ability to use AI to build routines.  Absolutely.

Love this app.

reviews.title: Not intuitive
reviews.text: This app has no consistency.  For starter, it’s confusing to start an exercise.  Is it start from the group set or the start button?  If u press the start button, it doesn’t start anything if you’re not looking at a set.   That begs the question what is the Start Exercise button for?  Then each exercise has a different way to start a “rest” time.   Some start automatically and some require the users to initiate.   Why is there a “log set a next exercise”  option when you just finished the first set?  I just wanna exercise and don’t want to fiddling on the app too much.
